briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Tops $17B in Sales as Tax-Relief Politics Heat Up; National Rescheduling and Psilocybin Momentum Build
briefs.top: Michigan's legal cannabis market just surpassed $17 billion in combined adult-use and medical marijuana sales, even as the state's 24% wholesale tax keeps bringing in only a fraction of what officials projected — and now has a gubernatorial front-runner and industry endorsement pushing repeal. Nationally, a federal court just backed marijuana's move to Schedule III, the DEA itself is arguing for reclassification, and Compass Pathways is mapping a 2027 psilocybin launch as fresh capital flows back into cannabis M&A.

local.text: Michigan crosses $17B in lifetime sales — August alone generated about $259 million, pushing cumulative adult-use and medical sales past $17 billion with roughly $2.66 billion in state taxes collected to date, per a new CRA report.

Industry group backs tax-repeal candidate — MiCIA officially endorsed GOP gubernatorial nominee John James over his pledge to repeal the 24% wholesale tax, giving operators a clear electoral path toward relief this November.

New Standard debuts in Ann Arbor — The chain opened its new Ann Arbor storefront with giveaways and discounts running through its opening weekend, adding fresh retail energy to a crowded local market.

Wholesale tax revenue keeps missing projections, fueling repeal push — The levy brought in roughly $34 million in Q1 and $37 million in Q2 versus a projected $105 million per quarter, adding momentum to a bipartisan repeal bill.

Rize's supplier deals show a path through the tax squeeze — While Higher Love shut five of its nine U.P. stores under the wholesale tax, Rize kept growing in the same region by negotiating cost-sharing arrangements that split the burden with suppliers.

national.text: Court upholds medical marijuana's move to Schedule III — A federal appeals court rejected a bid to block the reclassification, leaving the medical marijuana rescheduling order in effect as of September 9.

DEA itself argues for Schedule III — In its final post-hearing brief, the agency told the administrative law judge that cannabis no longer meets the criteria for Schedule I, a notable shift as the broader recreational rescheduling case heads toward a recommendation.

Compass Pathways eyes first-half 2027 psilocybin launch — At a Morgan Stanley healthcare conference, the company outlined its path to market after FDA granted a rolling NDA review and a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher for treatment-resistant depression.

State cannabis tax hauls jump 11% nationally — Q2 2026 marijuana tax collections hit $986.8 million, up 11% year-over-year and nearly 16% from Q1, per Census Bureau data, signaling continued market growth even amid state-level tax fights.

Vireo Growth's acquisition spree pays off — Revenue jumped 335% year-over-year to $209.3 million after buying Hawthorne, Eaze and Bridgewell, with fresh deals for FLUENT, C21 and a Planet 13 merger extending its footprint across Florida, Nevada and Illinois.
